interpretation_summary: The replication on the extended dataset supported the hypothesis with a significant negative difference in evolution endorsement between post-secular and traditional views. The replication closely followed the preregistration plan and was executed successfully.

fidelity_assessment.method_alignment: Full alignment: The replication used a weighted three-class categorical latent-class model and a pooled two-sided t-test as specified.

results_comparison.hypothesis_tested: Respondents with a post-secular perspective on science and religion will be less likely than respondents with a traditional perspective to respond that humans evolved from other animals.
results_comparison.original_results: Members of the post-secular category were significantly less likely than members of the traditional group to respond that humans evolved from other animals (3 percent, significant at p < 0.05).
results_comparison.replication_results: Post-secular evolution endorsement=0.038; traditional=0.408; difference=-0.370. Pooled two-sided t(1436)=-16.570, p=1.45e-56; conclusion=supported.
results_comparison.overall_answer: Yes, the replication results satisfy the preregistered comparison criteria for the claim.

replication_report: Replication successful: Post-secular evolution endorsement significantly lower than traditional, consistent with original findings.
notes: The replication was conducted on a different subset of the GSS dataset (2012–2018) compared to the original study years (2006–2010), but the results were consistent with the original findings.
